title: WPMS/2829/2016 of Harish Bhatt Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2829 of 2016
Harish Bhatt ÖÖ.Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ÖÖRespondents
Mr. Jagdish Singh Bisht, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand/ respondent nos.
1 & 4.
Mr. B.D. Upadhyaya, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. Naveen Tiwari, Advocate,
holding brief of Ms. Mamta Bisht, Advocate for the respondent nos. 2 & 3.
Dated: 21.11.2016
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.
 Petitioner has approached this Court seeking
the following relief:
ì(i.) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding the
respondents to re check/re-examine the
paper I, II & III of physics 2016 and
award the proper marks to the petitioner,
and further issue the proper mark sheet
to the petitioner after conducted and
awarded the proper marks for all papers
of physics 2016 B.Sc. II year, otherwise
the petitioner will suffer irreparably or
may please to pass such further order as
this Honíble Court may deem fit and
proper under these facts and
circumstances of the case. .î

2. Briefly put, the case of the petitioner is as
follows:
 In the year 2014-15, petitioner took admission
in B.Sc. I year (physics, chemistry and mathematics
group), as a regular student, at the Government Degree
College, Bazpur. Thereafter, the petitioner met with an
accident, which affected his studies of B.Sc. Ist year. The
petitioner appeared in the B.Sc. Ist year examination. In
the said examination, the petitioner was declared fail in
Chemistry and Mathematics. The petitioner applied for

2
the re-calculation of the Chemistry paper of B.Sc. Ist year.
After the re-calculation, petitioner was declared pass in
Chemistry examination. The petitioner appeared in the
improvement examination of Mathematics of B.Sc. Ist
year and, in the improvement examination, the petitioner
was declared pass in the month of January, 2016. In
the month of January, 2016, the petitioner took
admission in B.Sc. II year. In the month of April, 2016,
the petitioner appeared in the examination of B.Sc. II
year. The result of B.Sc. II year was declared in the
month of July, 2016 and the petitioner was declared fail
in physics and mathematics examination. It is alleged
that the marks given to the petitioner in physics (paper I,
II & III), according to the petitioner, was not correct,
hence, in the month of August, 2016, petitioner sought
answer sheets of Physics and Mathematics examination
from the University under the Right to Information Act.
The petitioner received the answer sheets under the Right
to Information Act in the Month of August-September,
2016. After perusal of the answer sheets of Physics
paper of B.S.C. II year and, after getting tallied his
answers with the textbook, the petitioner found that he
has not been awarded marks for the correct answers. It
is alleged that if the same is granted in a correct manner,
after re-checking/re-examining of answer sheets of the
petitioner for all papers of physics B.Sc. II year, 2016, the
petitioner would be declared pass in physics and he can
sit for the improvement examination for mathematics.
Thus, one year of the petitioner could be saved, if he was
declared pass in physics. Hence this writ petition.
3. Counter affidavit has been filed by the
respondent no. 2. In the counter affidavit, it is, inter alia,
stated as follows:

3
ì8. That the contents made in para 23 and
24 of the writ petition as stated are not correct,
hence denied. In reply, it is submitted that
University has provided the answer sheets to
the petitioner on his application under the
provisions of Right to Information Act, and in
case there was any mistake the petitioner was
having opportunity to represent before the
University so that the claim of the petitioner
may be verified from the subject expert.î
4. I have considered the submission made by the
learned counsel for the parties and have perused the
papers available on record.
5. Considering the facts mentioned in para 8 of
the counter affidavit, the writ petition is disposed of with
a direction that in case petitioner files a representation
ventilating his grievances before the University, the same
shall be decided by the competent Authority, in
accordance with law, within a period of 10 daysí from the
date of production of a certified copy of this judgment.
6. Let a certified copy of this judgment be issued
today itself.
